title: Conversational Compression — Product Brief & Launch Playbook
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Overview

Purpose: Introduce Conversational Compression, a product capability that reduces per-request token cost by applying a controlled, fidelity-aware compression layer to conversational inputs and short-term context while preserving user-visible quality. This brief summarizes motivations, target customers, success metrics, technical approaches, rollout plan, pricing implications, and early release notes.

Why this matters
- Production inference cost is dominated by input + context tokens for stateful conversational applications.
- Many real-world chat workflows have high redundancy: repeating system prompts, user rephrases, and long but low-information context.
- Controlled compression can reduce token volumes 20–60% for compatible workloads while keeping quality regressions within customer-acceptable bounds.

Who benefits
- High-frequency chatbots (transactional assistants, search-chat overlays).
- Multi-turn session stores where short-term context is noisy.
- Customers on Hosted and Dedicated who need predictable cost reduction without model changes.

Goals and non-goals
- Goals:
  1. Deliver a platform-level compression primitive that is model-agnostic and pluggable in the request path.
  2. Provide fidelity controls and per-route crediting to let customers trade cost vs. quality.
  3. Integrate with Optimize suggestions and Console telemetry for observability and guardrails.
- Non-goals:
  - Do not change underlying model weights or require retraining.
  - Not intended for long-term persistent vector store compression (separate product).

Key success metrics (first 6 months)
- Average token reduction for enabled tenants >= 30% (measured on production sampling).
- No-customer-visible quality regressions > 1.0% (user-reported intent failures).
- Adoption: 15% of eligible seats opt-in to auto-compression or enable via per-route flag.
- Cost impact: platform token spend reduction >= 6% across hosted fleet from opt-in.

High-level design
1) Compression modes (pluggable, selected per-route):
   - Truncate+: smart length-aware truncation retaining recent turns and extracted entities.
   - Semantic dedupe: detect and remove near-duplicate tokens/phrases across turns.
   - Paraphrase-normalize: lightweight rewrite of user/system text to canonical shorter forms.
   - Hybrid compress: combination of above with configurable aggressiveness (0–100).

2) Placement in request path:
   - Request ingress -> compression pipeline -> prompt assembler -> runtime.
   - Compression must run before tokenization to allow token-budget prediction and cost estimation.

3) Fidelity controls and safety:
   - Per-route fidelity budget (percentile-style): allow customers to set max allowed expected degradation and target token reduction.
   - Quality guardrails: mandatory safety checks to preserve PII, legal clauses, or user-specified "pin" segments which are not compressed.
   - Rollback policy: automatic revert to uncompressed request on fallback triggers (model perplexity spike, hallucination heuristics, customer manual rollback).

Configuration matrix (table)
Mode | Aggressiveness | Typical token reduction | Recommended use-cases | SLO impact
-----|----------------|------------------------|-----------------------|---------
Truncate+ | low/med/high | 8–35% | Short transactional assistants | low latency change
Semantic dedupe | med/high | 20–50% | Long multi-turn help desks, chat history trimming | low
Paraphrase-normalize | low/med | 10–30% | Mobile input normalization, shorter system prompts | potential slight quality variance
Hybrid | config-driven | 25–60% | High-volume chat workloads | monitored via telemetry

Telemetry and observability
- Telemetry hooks (Console integration):
  - Per-request token before/after, compression mode, aggressiveness, route id, tenant id.
  - Quality signals: rollbacks, perplexity delta, client-side user-declared failures.
  - Cost attribution: compressed_token_equivalent metric for billing pipeline.
- Dashboards: Compression adoption, token savings heatmap, top routes by savings, fidelity regression alerts.

SLOs and Safety thresholds
- Compression-induced latency budget: +30ms p50, +75ms p95 soft target for Hosted.
- Quality regression soft threshold: +0.5% intent-failure baseline; hard threshold +1.5% triggers auto-disable for route.
- Fallback frequency: <0.1% of compressed requests should trigger auto-revert.

Implementation considerations
- Runtime efficiency: implement compression in C++/Rust path used by request preprocessor to keep CPU overhead minimal; aim for <10ms median processing time for medium-length prompts (<=2k chars).
- Model-agnostic token estimation: use tokenizer-emulation library for major tokenizers (gpt2, llama, cl100k) to estimate token counts pre/post compression.
- Plugin architecture: compression strategies implemented as small strategy modules with metrics and tests; default strategies maintained by Redwood with override hooks for Dedicated/Private.
- Data residency: compression runs on-path; for Private/VPC deployments respect customer's data controls — run locally and never send compressed payloads to Redwood control plane unless explicitly opted-in.

Roadmap and milestones
- Q2 2026 (alpha): implement Truncate+ and semantic dedupe prototypes; internal lab experiments on real conversational prompt sets.
- Q3 2026 (private beta): route-level opt-in for Dedicated customers; Console telemetry and quality dashboard.
- Q4 2026 (hosted beta): public beta for Hosted tier with default disabled; Optimize suggestion integration.
- Q1 2027 (GA): pricing model announcement, SLA updates, SDK flags and migration docs.

Rollout playbook (numbered steps)
1. Internal canary (2 weeks): run compression on 0.5% sampled requests with telemetry only (no effect on runtime).
2. Shadow mode (4 weeks): compression applied but original payload also sent to runtime; compare outputs with offline diff metrics.
3. Controlled canary (6 weeks): enable compression for <1% traffic for selected tenants with opt-in flag; monitor metrics and customer feedback.
4. Private beta: onboard 5–10 Dedicated customers via solutions engineering with API toggles and SLA addendum.
5. Hosted beta opt-in: open sign-up with per-route controls and migration template.
6. GA: enable programmatic opt-in paths, pricing and invoicing changes, and public docs.

Pricing and packaging considerations
- Billing unit: compressed_token_equivalent — bill customers on their effective token consumption after compression as reported by platform metrics.
- Pricing modes (provisional):
  - Mode A (pass-through): customers pay per compressed token at standard per-token rates.
  - Mode B (subscription uplift): flat subscription tier for "Compression Pro" that includes higher aggressiveness thresholds and priority support; may include a small percentage surcharge for aggressive modes that warrant extra telemetry.
  - Credits & trials: include a trial bucket of compression credits during beta.
- Commercial guardrails: ensure transparency — show token-before/token-after and estimated savings on invoices for first 3 months post-GA to avoid billing disputes.

Customer-facing docs and SDK changes
- New SDK flags: compression.mode, compression.aggressiveness, compression.pinned_segments.
- Console UX: per-route toggle, recommendation wizards from Optimize, and a migration checklist.
- Quickstart: sample flows for chat assistants, recommended aggressiveness by workload.

Open questions (for prioritization)
- How to price aggressive paraphrase-normalize modes that may require additional human QA for high-risk legal/regulatory text?
- For Dedicated/Private, offer operator controls vs. Redwood-managed defaults — what’s the right tradeoff for customers who want turnkey savings?
- Should compression be subject to separate SLA for accuracy degradation?

Release notes (preview)
- 2026-05-20 — Alpha release notes:
  - Introduced Conversational Compression alpha prototypes: Truncate+ and Semantic Dedupe.
  - Console telemetry hooks available under feature-flag.
  - Internal experiments show median token reduction of 28% on sampled partner workloads.

Appendix: example CLI and JSON configuration
- Example API request (JSON) with compression flags:
  {
    \"route\": \"chat/assistant-v1\",
    \"compression\": {\"mode\": \"hybrid\", \"aggressiveness\": 50, \"pinned_segments\": [\"legal-disclaimer\"]},
    \"input\": \"[user messages and context here]\"
  }

- CLI: enable compression for route
  redwood routes update chat/assistant-v1 --compression-mode=hybrid --compression-aggressiveness=50

Related reading
- Observability: see \"observability-cost-latency-tradeoffs-guide\"
- Quantization & fidelity experiments: see PRD for quantization-fidelity experimentation lab

Notes
- This brief focuses on short-term context and live request compression. Persistent store compaction and embedding-level compression remain separate initiatives.
